record.kind: marker passive with no PassiveEffects entry; behaviour is driven by four nectar items' OnItemDroppedEffects, the flower-pot drop command and each form's onAcquired
record.summary: Passive.NECTAR has no PassiveEffects entry and no combat effect. It marks the four Oricorio forms. Each nectar item has an OnItemDroppedEffect: dropping RED_NECTAR on a NECTAR unit turns it into ORICORIO_BAILE, YELLOW_NECTAR into ORICORIO_POMPOM, PINK_NECTAR into ORICORIO_PA_U and PURPLE_NECTAR into ORICORIO_SENSU (nothing happens if it already is that form), and the item is never equipped (the handler returns false). Nectars are supplied through flower pots: when a flower pot finishes growing, a nectar of the pot's colour (BLUE pot -> PURPLE, PINK -> RED, WHITE -> PINK, YELLOW -> YELLOW) is added to the player's items if absent, once per NECTAR unit on the board; and acquiring an Oricorio form (including through transformPokemon) calls giveNectarsAlreadyUnlocked to add the nectars for pots that are already finished. Every form's skill is REVELATION_DANCE; stats, range and types come from the class.
triggers: Dragging a nectar item onto a unit with passive NECTAR (OnItemDroppedEffect)
A flower pot reaching the end of its growth via mulch drop (nectar granted if an Oricorio form is on the board)
Player acquiring an Oricorio form (onAcquired) including via transformPokemon

effects.declaredRaw: nectar colour selects the target form: RED->BAILE, YELLOW->POMPOM, PINK->PA_U, PURPLE->SENSU
effects.scaling: none (no AP, no crit, no combat effect)
effects.resolution: transformPokemon creates the new form from PokemonFactory, carries over permanent stats, dishes, position and held items, then runs the new form's onAcquired and updateSynergies

effects.declaredRaw: one nectar per finished flower pot, granted when absent
effects.resolution: flower-pot drop command and giveNectarsAlreadyUnlocked push the item only if player.items lacks it

conditions: The dropped-on unit must have passive NECTAR; otherwise the handler does nothing and still returns false (no unit ever holds a nectar).
Dropping the nectar of the form the unit already is does not transform it.

The pot-to-nectar mapping in the command (BLUE/PINK/WHITE/YELLOW) and the pot-index order in the helper (RED, YELLOW, PINK, PURPLE) are written separately in the source; this record does not equate the two orders beyond what the lines show.
Transformation is a pick-phase action, not tied to fights.
record.resetBehaviour: No counter or stored state; the form is the state. Nectars stay in player.items until used (the lines read never remove them; a nectar is not consumed by the drop because the item is not equipped and the cancel path is taken).
